comparator.name: Chemistry
comparator.route: Chemistry of Life specialisation with University Minor
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally adopted 2026–2027 Chemistry regulations account for the full 180 EC. Year 1 is twelve compulsory 5-EC courses. The remaining 120 EC comprise ten further compulsory 5-EC chemistry courses, one 20-EC specialization, a 5-EC Research Practical, a 15-EC Bachelor Research Project and a 30-EC minor. The generic target offers Chemistry of Life, Smart Materials, and Sustainable Chemistry and Energy. No option is clearly more general, so Chemistry of Life is selected by the formal regulations’ official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit. The genuine 30-EC University Minor remains open choice space. The live programme page and formally adopted 2026–2027 Chemistry regulations were rechecked on 2026-10-14; the settled specialization, open minor and 180-EC reconstruction remain unchanged.

routeSelection.route: Chemistry of Life specialisation with University Minor
routeSelection.basis: The generic Chemistry target offers three formally named 20-EC specialisations. Current official evidence does not establish one as more representative or less specialised than the others, so the first specialisation in the formally adopted 2026–2027 regulations, Chemistry of Life, is selected as the neutral tie-break. The University Minor preserves the regulated open 30-EC minor space. Neither choice is based on UCR fit.

core: Molecular structure, biochemistry, cellular mechanisms and Chemistry of Life applications
Biomedical function, disease, pharmacology and molecular health research as related applications of molecular science
Mathematics, programming, modelling and statistical analysis for molecular and material questions
Laboratory experimentation and independent scientific inquiry
Materials, energy, sustainability, catalysis, resources and environmental consequences of chemical systems
questions: How do molecular and biochemical processes produce biological function, disease and treatment possibilities?
How can molecular and biomedical questions be investigated experimentally and quantitatively?
How can materials, energy and resource systems be studied for sustainability and environmental improvement?

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & biomedical life sciences
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, laboratory work, genetics, disease, pharmacology and quantitative analysis form the visible spine; the title does not imply a chemistry degree.
alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular life through biochemistry, physiology, genetics, immunity, disease, laboratory work, pharmacology and quantitative analysis. This is the strongest complete related-fields response to the selected Chemistry of Life specialisation; it does not reproduce general, organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or quantum chemistry, spectroscopy, synthesis or specialist chemistry laboratories.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming, mathematics, statistics and data foundations precede molecular biology, physiology, laboratory work, genetics, disease, immunity, pharmacology and advanced analysis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Biochemistry, environmental materials & quantitative science
alternatives.concept: Combine biochemistry and molecular-cell study with environmental geochemistry, soils, resource recovery, material life cycles, Earth resources and renewable systems, using laboratory, mathematical, programming, statistical and modelling methods. This route addresses sustainable-materials and environmental-chemistry interests but does not teach synthetic, organic, analytical or physical chemistry.
alternatives.labelReason: Four molecular or biochemical courses, twelve environmental, Earth, materials and sustainability courses, and seven mathematics, programming, data and research courses support the three stated strands in proportion.
progression: Sustainability, Earth-science, programming, mathematical and research foundations precede molecular biology, biochemistry, laboratory work, geochemical analysis, material recovery, resource study, renewable-system design and advanced quantitative work. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; six courses are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme centres molecular, cellular and biomedical biology, pharmacology, disease and computational analysis. This route centres environmental geochemistry, materials, resources, circularity and energy systems. The programmes share nine courses and each contains fifteen courses, or 112.5 EC, absent from the other.

candidates.label: Biochemistry, environmental materials and quantitative science

selection.assessment: The molecular, cellular and biomedical programme is the strongest complete related-fields response to the selected Chemistry of Life route and its molecular, medicinal, laboratory and quantitative interests. Materials, sustainable energy and environmental applications support a substantially distinct second route through biochemistry, Earth materials, geochemistry, circularity, resources and quantitative science; the two routes differ by fifteen courses (112.5 EC) each. The next direction, synthetic, inorganic and physical chemistry, fails because UCR lacks the required cumulative chemistry, synthesis, spectroscopy, chemical-analysis and specialist laboratory sequence. Production stops at two.

blocks: Both address molecules and their functions; UCR introduces biomolecules inside life science rather than teaching general molecular structure and reactivity.
Both directly study biomolecules, metabolism and biochemical mechanisms; UCR does so within life science rather than a chemistry sequence.
Molecular Cell Biology directly studies cellular molecules, gene expression and signalling, while not reproducing the comparator’s chemistry framing.

The UCR laboratory includes bacterial techniques, protein production, DNA analysis and bioinformatics, directly overlapping recombinant-DNA and biotechnology practice while remaining one broad life-science laboratory.
Pharmacology directly studies molecular drug targets, therapeutic action and toxicity, addressing an applied part of chemical biology without reproducing its chemistry foundation.
Both address bioenergy; UCR analyses renewable-system design and performance rather than metabolism and bioresource chemistry.
Both provide mathematical foundations for scientific study; UCR is a broad methods course rather than chemistry-specific mathematics.
Advanced Calculus directly develops multivariable calculus and differential equations, while the comparator component also integrates linear algebra for chemistry.

The comparator’s chemistry-specific ethical and professional component remains unmatched; generic academic orientation is not presented as chemistry training.

UCR has no advanced chemical or biochemical synthesis-and-analysis sequence.
UCR offers laboratory and applied research courses, but no staged chemistry research practical.
The compulsory experimental Chemistry research project remains visible; UCR’s standardized optional independent-research opportunity is shown here without claiming a scheduled equivalent.
The genuine 30-EC University Minor remains open; no fixed UCR content is invented for it.

notes.text: Groningen Chemistry requires cumulative general, organic, inorganic, physical and quantum chemistry, spectroscopy, transport phenomena, materials, synthesis and analysis laboratories, specialist chemistry study and an experimental research project. UCR can combine molecular and biomedical life science with quantitative methods, or pursue biochemistry, environmental materials and sustainable resource systems. These are coherent related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the Chemistry curriculum.

The external programme has a fixed chemistry and laboratory core, a 20-EC specialisation, a research practical, a 15-EC chemistry research project and a genuine 30-EC minor. UCR assembles adjacent sciences across individually selected 7.5-EC courses and offers no scheduled specialist chemistry thesis or staged chemistry laboratory sequence.
